page: Amazon Web Services t2.nano is an entry-level burstable instance deployed on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.4 GHz, provisioned with 1 burstable vCPU, 1 physical core, and a 32 KB L1d, 0.25 MB L2, and 45 MB L3 cache configuration. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance contains 0.5 GB of system memory, does not include a GPU, lacks bundled local storage, and features a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight constrained compute and throughput capacities consistent with its resource profile. The single-core stress-ng score reaches 1850.89, placing it in the average middle 50% category. However, because it relies on a single vCPU, the multi-core stress-ng score remains identical at 1850.89, falling into the bottom 10%. PassMark CPU testing yields an overall score of 1428.49, with extended instructions scoring 898.71, encryption at 483.54, and physics at 210.47, all placing in the bottom 10%. Memory read bandwidth on cached small blocks reaches 76.09 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations handle 0.52 million operations per second and static web serving achieves 1.1 GB/sec throughput, both residing in the lowest decile.

The primary tradeoff of the t2.nano is its minimal footprint and burstable CPU allocation model. While it provides an extremely cost-efficient footprint for intermittent and background processes, continuous sustained compute will exhaust CPU credits. With only 0.5 GB of RAM and reliance on remote storage, this server is suitable exclusively for low-traffic microservices, lightweight monitoring daemons, bastion hosts, and small development or test utilities.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.nano is an entry-level, burstable general-purpose instance featuring 1 burstable vCPU and 0.5 GB of RAM powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz. Deployed on the Xen hypervisor, it includes AVX and AES-NI extensions with a 45 MB L3 cache, but includes no local storage or dedicated GPU. In benchmarks, the instance delivers average single-core stress-ng performance at 1850.89, but drops into the bottom 10% across multi-core and PassMark suites due to its single-threaded limit and minimal memory capacity. Static web throughput reaches 1.1 GB/sec and Redis SET performance registers 0.52 million operations per second. Lacking bundled local storage and baseline networking throughput, t2.nano provides a cost-efficient resource profile suited for low-traffic web endpoints, simple background scripts, and lightweight administrative utilities.
